newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon M3 money up 1.53 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon M3 money up 1.53 pct in April.

text.p: Lebanon's M3 money supply grew in April by 1.53 percent to 30,833 billion pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said on Tuesday.

"M3 growth was considered moderate during April. This growth was mainly due to the increase in net credits to the public sector and the rise in credits to the private sector," the bank said in its latest monthly report on the economy.
M3 recorded an annual growth of 27.4 percent compared with 27.38 percent at the end of March, the bank said.

It said the rate of growth of M3 declined due to the deficit in the balance of payments and the appreciation of the Lebanese pound against the dollar in the foreign exchange market but gave no further details.
M1 money stock registered monthly and annual growth of 1.22 percent and 16.15 percent respectively, the bank said.
M2 an M4 registered respective annual growths of 45.92 percent and 31.37 percent, the bank added.

"The Lebanese pound component of liquidity (M2) continued its sustained annual growth reaching 45.92 percent in April against 43.12 in March and 41.40 in February, reflecting continuous shift towards savings in Lebanese pounds. M2 represented 49.64 percent of liquidity," the bank said.
It issued the following statistics (blns of Lebanese pounds at end of period):
M1 M2 M3 M4
The Bank defined the aggregates as follows:
M1 -- Currency in circulation + Demand deposits
M2 -- M1 + Other deposits in Lebanese pounds
M3 -- M2 + Deposits in F.X.
M4 -- M3 + Treasury bills held by the non-banking system
($1= 1,543.5 at the end of April)
